transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-02
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Raj Patel (Redwood SE), Nora Li (Redwood CSM); Evelyn Ortiz (SynergyXR Head of ML), Devin Park (Platform Eng), Liam O'Connor (CTO), Marta (Data Eng)

Summary:
Quick sync on pilot economics: tokens/sec/$, caching wins from prefix + KV, batching tradeoffs vs tail latency, and next steps for a focused benchmark. Agreed to run two benchmark profiles and share updated cost model.

Topics:
- current pilot metrics and pain points
- caching vs batching (savings and latency impacts)
- quantization and model variant tradeoffs
- infra constraints (VPC, private deployment timeline)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick roll call?
[00:05] Evelyn Ortiz: hey Evelyn here.
[00:07] Devin Park: Devin.
[00:09] Liam: Liam.
[00:10] Marta: Marta.
[00:12] Raj Patel: Raj from Redwood, morning all.
[00:15] Maya Chen: cool, so objective today is to review the last week of pilot results and decide tuning for tokens-per-dollar. I have the cost spreadsheet up, I'll share after.

[02:05] Devin Park: quick context — our workload is heavy on short prompts with a standard 1-3 turn chat, average 120 tokens in, 200 tokens out. Peaks at roughly 220 qps during business hours. Right now we're seeing about 0.95 tokens/sec/$ — which feels off, we thought we'd get closer to 3 tokens per dollar with caching.

[03:22] Raj Patel: ok a couple notes — first, the run we saw had prefix caching disabled for safety; enabling prefix/K V cache (sometimes calls it K-V cash on the logs) should improve tokens/sec/$ significantly on repeated templates. We estimated 2–2.8x improvement for your traffic mix.

[04:10] Evelyn Ortiz: yeah, we were nervous about cache consistency and data residency — our prompts sometimes contain PII-like customer ids.

[04:35] Nora Li: quick note on that — Redwood's prefix masking + deterministic hash policy can redact identifiers before caching; we ran a similar pattern with another retail customer. We'll send the design doc.

[05:06] Liam: timing — also want to understand the latency impact. If batching helps cost but increases p95 beyond our SLO of 350ms, that's a problem.

[06:01] Raj Patel: totally. Batching improves tokens/sec/$ because of amortized kernel launch overheads, but it increases tail latency for single-request flows. We can do dynamic batching windows and target a 50ms batch wait to keep tail in check. For your peak qps we expect batching to add ~30–60ms p95 if we push aggressive batch sizes.

[07:22] Marta: curious about quantization — you mentioned q4_0 vs int8; what's realistic for our accuracy bar?

[07:40] Raj Patel: we've onboarded two variants — q4_0 (float-ish quant) keeps quality within 1–2% on rouge/bleu for generative prompts, int8 can shave more cost but may degrade scoring for long-context completions. For your short chat flows q4_0 is probably safe. We'll provide a short evaluation pack.

[09:05] Evelyn Ortiz: can you remind us of the tokens/sec/$ math? I lost the thread.

[09:12] Maya Chen: sure — high level: tokens/sec/$ is measured by total tokens served divided by total cost in a timeframe; when we talk tokens/sec/$ per model variant it's the slope as we change batch sizes and caching. On your baseline without caching we measured ~0.95 tokens/sec/$, with prefix caching enabled and q4_0 we project ~2.4 tokens/sec/$. If you add 2x batching (medium window) we could reach ~3.1 tokens/sec/$ but expect tail latency tradeoffs.

[11:45] Devin Park: the raw logs show a high percent of identical starting prompts — maybe 38% are templated. So cache should matter.

[12:18] Raj Patel: exactly — with caching, the KV cache reuses past key/value states for repeated prefixes so generation cost drops dramatically; also prefix caching avoids recomputing early tokens. Note: need to be careful about recency — for dynamic customer context we recommend TTL of 15 minutes.

[14:02] Liam: what's the deployment plan? If we go Private (VPC), how long to stand up and does that affect benchmarks?

[14:22] Nora Li: Private deployment typically takes 2–3 weeks for integration with your KMS and SSO. For the benchmarking we can run hosted isolated pool first; results port over but dedicated infra variance is +/- 5–10% depending on instance types.

[16:00] Marta: we also have compliance questions — audit logs, retention, and where cached bits live.

[16:20] Maya Chen: we'll share the security whitepaper; logs and cache can be encrypted at rest and access-controlled. For sensitive fields we suggest redaction before hitting cache.

[18:05] Evelyn Ortiz: ok good. On the economics test: can you run two benchmark profiles? One that optimizes for latency (low batching, small window, caching on) and one for throughput (bigger batch windows, aggressive caching, q4_0).

[18:40] Raj Patel: yes, we'll do that. Proposal:
- Latency profile: batch wait <=30ms, dynamic batching, prefix caching TTL 5m, q4_0 single replica.
- Throughput profile: batch wait 150ms, larger batch cap, prefix + KV caching TTL 15m, q4_0 + optional int8 trial.

[19:55] Devin Park: makes sense. Please include token-level cost breakdown and tokens/sec/$ curves per profile.

[21:10] Maya Chen: we'll include a chart and the raw numbers. Also, we'll run a 48h throughput run overnight to capture diurnal variance.

[22:30] Evelyn Ortiz: a question on fallbacks — if the model variant fails or latency spikes do you have graceful fallback to smaller model?

[22:48] Raj Patel: yes, smart routing can fall back to a lower-cost model variant with a fast path but we'll surface accuracy deltas. We can configure per-route fallbacks and a canary rollout.

[24:01] Liam: any mention of competitor tradeoffs? We briefly evaluated InferStack and CloudAI; InferStack gave better latency at single-core but poorer batching efficiency, CloudAI had hidden egress costs.

[24:30] Maya Chen: thanks — we'll include a competitor comparison note in the follow-up.

[25:12] Nora Li: action item recap coming in a sec. Also we noticed your traffic spikes are concentrated Mon-Fri 9–11am; consider warm-up strategies to prime caches before peak.

[26:05] Marta: what's warm-up look like — a synthetic ramp?

[26:15] Raj Patel: usually a short synthetic burst of templated requests to populate K V cache and model context; takes 5–10 minutes to be effective.

[28:00] Evelyn Ortiz: one concern — if we use prefix masking are we confident it won't leak customer identifiers into the cache keys?

[28:20] Raj Patel: the deterministic hash with scrubbing ensures masked tokens are replaced before caching; we have a test harness we'll run against your sample prompts.

[30:12] Devin Park: ok, for the benchmark please also capture p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1M tokens.

[31:00] Maya Chen: noted. We'll send a template for the prompt family and the traffic profile.

[33:15] Evelyn Ortiz: timeline recap?

[33:20] Maya Chen: we'll run the benchmarks and share results by Friday 2026-03-06. Raj will hand over logs and the spreadsheet. You (SynergyXR) will share sample prompts and traffic distribution by Wednesday 2026-03-04. Then we'll do a technical deep dive next week for VPC/KMS.

[35:40] Liam: any quick wins we can apply immediately?

[35:48] Raj Patel: enable prefix caching for templated prompts and switch to q4_0 variant will be the fastest wins — expected 2x tokens/sec/$. Also adjust batch wait to 50ms to balance SLO.

[37:10] Marta: can you annotate the spreadsheet showing the delta per change?

[37:18] Maya Chen: yes, I'll annotate each row with 'before' and 'after' projections.

[39:00] Devin Park: small nit — in earlier logs some requests were mis-attributed and showed as Speaker 1 in raw traces; that'll make parsing harder, but we can map by request-id.

[39:30] Raj Patel: noted, we'll include request-id mapping in logs.

[42:05] Evelyn Ortiz: ok one last thing — billing model: if we go to Dedicated later, how does committed capacity change tokens/sec/$?

[42:24] Nora Li: Dedicated typically improves unit economics by 15–30% depending on commitment level and instance selection. We'll model both hosted and dedicated scenarios in the spreadsheet.

[44:10] Liam: perfect. Sounds like a plan.

[45:00] Maya Chen: recap of next steps — I'll read them out: 1) Redwood to run two benchmarks (latency/throughput) and share charts + raw logs by 2026-03-06; 2) SynergyXR to share prompt families and traffic profile by 2026-03-04; 3) Redwood to send security/arch whitepaper and prefix masking design doc; 4) schedule deep-dive for VPC/KMS week of 2026-03-09.

[46:30] Evelyn Ortiz: agreed.
[46:40] Devin Park: agreed.
[46:42] Maya Chen: cool thanks all, we'll follow up in email with the spreadsheet. End call.
